newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees foreign bank legislation by December.
newsitem.headline: Canada sees foreign bank legislation by December.

text.p: The Canadian government plans to introduce legislation by the end of the year to further open up Canadian banking to foreign bank branches, junior minister Jim Peterson said on Wednesday.
Peterson was sworn in on Wednesday as secretary of state for financial institutions for Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien's second term.

"The foreign branching has already been recommended and announced by the previous (Chretien) government, and we expect to see legislation by the year end, which will creat a lot more competition here in Canada for our domestic banks," Peterson told reporters after a cabinet planning session.
He said he hoped one benefit would be for small businesses that had not had access to credit.
Asked about his direction in terms of regulation, he said: "We want a highly competitive financial services industry in Canda, where consumers have choice.
"We want one that offers benefits to consumers, to individual small businesses...We want an industry which is booming and which is expanding and growing and creating jobs."
Several questions would have to await an advisory panel report, however, he said: the issues of banks entering the insurance business, bank mergers and overall deregulation.
Peterson, who in the last Parliament chaired the House of Commons Finance Committee, held out little hope for banks getting an end to the surtax on their profits.
"We're sure that will arise in pre-budget hearings, and every budget that comes up. But I don't envisage that will be a major priority (for the government)," he said.
